# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Saturday, November 28, 2026

Weekend edition for Saturday 28 November 2026 (IST), covering Friday 27 November to Saturday morning; data compiled 07:00–07:45 IST. **This is a weekend edition carrying Friday's close: NSE, BSE, currency and bond markets are shut today, Saturday has no Indian session of its own, and no figure below is a live number.** The latest completed session is Friday 27 November 2026, and every index, stock, currency and bullion figure below is that session's. IBJA prints no weekend rate — its own page message reads "Rates are not published on Central Govt. Holidays & SAT/SUN" — so the domestic benchmark below is **Friday's PM session, labelled as such**, and no Saturday bullion figure exists to carry. **AGLOC's page this morning carries a new block headed 30 November 2026 and dated 28-30 November on its own table, so it covers this weekend and Monday; its reference is Friday's own close, so it is not a weekend print and no weekend rate is called live anywhere in this report.** The Sensex is a BSE index and its figure comes from a market source — The HinduBusinessLine's closing report, corroborated by News On AIR — never the NSE archive. Each block below keeps its own as-of date — Friday's PM print, Friday's settlements and closes, AGLOC's 28-30 November block, the 23:55 board stamp — and no rate is described as current beyond its own stamp. Saturday is a two-report day — news and regulation; the weekly analysis desk files on Mondays, and nothing weekly is due today.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Gold turns up hard, and the gold-loan names are the only part of the financial complex that closed higher — one session, not a trend
The collateral picture reversed direction on Friday. **Front-month Comex gold for December delivery — the new front month — settled at $3,639.60 an ounce, up $103.80 or 2.94% on the day and 3.53% on the week** (Dow Jones Market Data via Morningstar, 27 November). **Comex silver for December settled at $43.167 an ounce, up $3.109 or 7.76% on the day and 5.11% on the week** — and the same silver series struck its **52-week low of $40.052 on 25 November, two sessions before Friday's settle**. The domestic benchmark moved with it. **IBJA's 27 November PM session put 916 at ₹1,15,690 per 10 g, up ₹3,351 or 2.98% PM-to-PM, and 999 at ₹1,26,299, up ₹3,658 or 2.98%; silver 999 rose ₹6,953 or 4.72% to ₹1,54,300 a kg.** The full PM set: 995 at ₹1,25,793, 750 at ₹94,724, 585 at ₹73,885, platinum at ₹47,740. Both agency feeds agree with IBJA to the rupee: **PTI's Mumbai bullion closing rate prints silver at 1,54,300.00 a kg, and News On AIR reported at 18:11 IST that 24-carat gold surged three per cent to 1,26,299 rupees per 10 grams and silver 4.7 per cent to 1,54,300 rupees a kilogram, both per IBJA's closing rates.** Within the day, the PM session sat above the AM on both metals: 916 ₹1,15,690 against ₹1,14,789, 999 ₹1,26,299 against ₹1,25,316, silver ₹1,54,300 against ₹1,53,275 (the AM session printed 995 at ₹1,24,814, 750 at ₹93,987, 585 at ₹73,310, platinum at ₹47,540). IBJA's own daily PDF, filed under the header "Date: 27th November 2026", actually tabulates the **26 November** AM/PM columns (999 AM 1,22,982 / PM 1,22,641; 916 AM 1,12,652 / PM 1,12,339; silver PM 1,47,347) and its footer reads "as of 26th November 2026" — so it corroborates the Previous cells used below, not Friday's print. Friday's numbers come from the IBJA history table itself, cross-checked to PTI and News On AIR.

**The divergence is the story.** Friday was a broad risk-off session in Indian equities — the indices are in the markets section below — and inside it the gold-collateral names were bought: **Muthoot Finance closed at ₹2,609.50, up ₹51.50 or 2.01%; Manappuram at ₹278.40, up ₹8.40 or 3.11%; IIFL Finance at ₹598.50, up ₹4.55 or 0.77% — on a day the Nifty 50 fell 1.07% to 25,607.20 and Nifty Financial Services fell 1.33% to 28,337.15.** Livemint's market report (10:25 IST, intraday) recorded the same split as it happened — gold finance stocks rallying as bullion rebounded from a more-than-one-year low, Muthoot Finance up as much as 3.7% intraday, Manappuram 3%, IIFL 2.3% — and the reading is mechanical, not psychological: **the gold-loan lenders were bought because the collateral they lend against became more valuable on the same day the wider financial complex was sold.**

What Friday is not: a trend, or a recovery. It is one session. The Comex silver series that settled at $43.167 on Friday struck its 52-week low two sessions earlier, on 25 November; the domestic 916 PM series ran ₹1,14,450 on 23 November, ₹1,10,871 on 25 November, ₹1,12,339 on 26 November and ₹1,15,690 on Friday, and the silver series ₹1,52,625, ₹1,42,945, ₹1,47,347 and ₹1,54,300 — Friday is the second consecutive up-print on each domestic series, with the 25 November fall one place below it. **The pack prints no peak reference for this cycle and no 52-week low for the Comex gold series, so neither is constructed here; the size of the correction is carried only in the loan-book reporting the next story covers.** Nothing in Friday's move is extrapolated forward.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a higher gold price raises the collateral value behind gold loans across lenders, including Muthoot Fincorp, on every ticket at once. The equity moves belong to the listed companies whose tickers printed them — Muthoot Finance, Manappuram and IIFL Finance are listed peers — and Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted, with no share price in either index; nothing about the company's own book is inferred from Friday's session.

### Friday's rally does not fix the LTV arithmetic — the books were written near the peak, and one up-session does not re-write them
The reporting published across Thursday and Friday measures the loan books against the collateral fall, and none of it says the fall has been worked off. **The Economic Times (26 November, 05:30 IST) reports that thresholds were breached in nearly 40% of gold-loan portfolios, with the ratio crossing 95% in some cases**, that gold finance companies have started issuing legal auction notices, and that **gold auctions are held 30 days after serving a legal notice**. In the gold-loan business an LTV breach is deemed a default even where no repayment obligation has been missed — the standing maintenance rule, carried with its bands in the regulation report. ET also reports, in its own sourcing, that **banks and lenders have told the RBI they have lowered the LTV on fresh loans to an average of 60–65% from about 75%** — a representation to the regulator, written here exactly as reported: the RBI has not relaxed or cut anything, and where fresh loans are being written below the bands is prudential discretion, not a requirement on any named company.

The arithmetic of the fall, as published. **Moneycontrol (27 November, 17:15 IST) reports that a loan written at 70% LTV near the peak is now worth about 103% of its collateral, and that bullet-repayment loans carry the most risk** — on Moneycontrol's own two figures, the collateral behind such a loan has fallen to roughly two-thirds of the price it was written against. Moneycontrol also reports bank gold-loan growth of 83% year-on-year in October — the growth that wrote the book now being managed down. **BusinessLine (26 November, 20:41 IST) reports that portfolio LTVs at some gold-loan NBFCs have crossed 75%, with certain segments possibly having breached 85%, and loans originated at 80–85% LTV now standing at 90–95%**, the lenders shifting into collection mode rather than growth mode. **The asymmetry is arithmetic, not opinion: Friday's 2.98% PM-to-PM rise in the 916 rate recovers a small part of a fall of that size, not the fall itself — and AGLOC's new block, below, re-strikes the reference to Friday's close for the 28-30 November window; it is the same price applied forward, not new collateral value.** Moneycontrol's 103% figure was published Friday evening, 17:15 IST, and the pack does not state which session's prices it measures; it is carried as Moneycontrol's, not restated as any book's position.

Antique Stock Broking's view, as reported by Livemint on 27 November and attributed here as a brokerage view: **the 1QFY27 disbursement vintage has nearly breached the regulatory LTV limit at current prices, and a further 21% correction in gold prices across the loan tenure could cause recovery losses on that vintage.** Antique's ratings in the same report — **'Buy' on Manappuram with the target cut to ₹370, 'Hold' on Muthoot Finance at ₹2,650** — are calls on two listed peers, not on this company.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the ongoing-LTV maintenance the reporting describes applies across gold-loan lenders, including Muthoot Fincorp. No public document states where the company's own book sits against the bands, how many notices it has served, or what share of its portfolio originated above 60% LTV, and none of that is inferred. The 60–65% fresh-loan figure is an industry representation reported by ET; the nearly-40%, 103%, 75%/85% and 90–95% figures belong to ET, Moneycontrol and BusinessLine respectively, and none is restated as a fact about any named company's book.

### AGLOC's new block runs 28–30 November and is headed 30 November — a mechanical re-strike of Friday's close, not new price discovery
**AGLOC's page this morning carries a new block whose own heading reads "for 30th Nov 2026" and whose date row runs 28/11/2026 - 30/11/2026, so it covers this weekend and Monday rather than Monday alone: a jewellery reference of ₹11,569 a gram (the page prints "on Gold Jewellery price of Rs 11569 /-"), with the bands at ₹9,833 at 85% LTV, ₹9,255 at 80% and ₹8,676 at 75%.** Against the block whose date row is 27/11/2026 - 27/11/2026 — the one carried in Friday's edition — reference ₹11,233, bands ₹9,548 / ₹8,987 / ₹8,425 — that is **+₹336 on the reference, +₹285 at the 85% band, +₹268 at 80% and +₹251 at 75%**, and the percentages on those moves (+2.99% on the reference, +2.98% on each band) are arithmetic on AGLOC's own two blocks, because the page states rupee figures only.

Two facts state what this block is. **First: the reference ₹11,569 equals IBJA's 27 November PM 916 rate divided by ten exactly — ₹1,15,690 ÷ 10 = ₹11,569.** That equality makes the block a mechanical re-strike of Friday afternoon's close carried into this weekend and Monday: **a fresh block, but not new price action, and not independent price discovery.** **Second: the three bands are fixed percentages of the one reference — 0.85 × 11,569 = 9,833.65, printed 9,833; 0.80 × 11,569 = 9,255.2, printed 9,255; 0.75 × 11,569 = 8,676.75, printed 8,676 — so the bands' identical +2.98% moves are one observation, not three.** Because the reference is Friday's own close, nothing in this block is a weekend discovery; IBJA prints no weekend rate, so the next domestic benchmark that can move on its own is Monday's session.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the operative ceiling the company lends under is ₹9,833 a gram at the 85% band for the block running 28-30 November, ₹285 above the previous block, with the higher bands moving in lockstep; the block is a market print inside the standing rulebook, not a rule move, and nothing about the company's own book is inferred from it.
Sources: [AGLOC, block headed 30 Nov 2026 and dated 28-30 Nov on its own table, read 28 Nov 07:01 IST](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/)

### The Friday session: a broad risk-off close, a weaker rupee, oil down on the day and up on the week, and the flows behind it
Every index and stock figure in this section is Friday 27 November's close, from the NSE's own files for the date; the Sensex is a BSE index, cited to The HinduBusinessLine's closing report, never the NSE archive. **The Nifty 50 closed at 25,607.20, down 277.30 points or 1.07%; Nifty Bank at 63,040.90, down 494.40 or 0.78%; Nifty Financial Services at 28,337.15, down 381.75 or 1.33%; Nifty Financial Services 25/50 at 30,279.70, down 369.75 or 1.21%; Nifty 500 at 23,949.35, down 137.15 or 0.57%. The Sensex — the BSE print — closed at 83,339.26, down 989.33 or 1.17%** (The HinduBusinessLine, 27 November, 19:29 IST, under the headline "Sensex sheds 989 points as crude, rupee end four-week Nifty rally"; corroborated by News On AIR at 18:06 IST). BusinessLine's framing — crude and the rupee ending a four-week Nifty rally — is the market source's own read of the session, carried attributed rather than adopted. The pack carries no VIX, midcap or smallcap figure for the session, so none appears here.

The currency and the crude behind that headline: **the rupee settled at 92.98 against the US dollar, a provisional close, 60 paise weaker than the previous close of 92.38** (PTI via The Hindu, 27 November, 16:51 IST, updated 17:28 IST; PTI's wire copy also ran as "62 paise to 93" and "60 paise to 93" — the settled figure in all versions is 92.98 or 92.99, and 92.98 is used here, labelled provisional, without averaging the variants). PTI's copy records the open and the day's low but no high, so no high-low range is stated here for the session, and none is carried. **Front-month ICE Brent for January delivery settled at $95.44 a barrel, down $1.13 or 1.2% on the day, still up 3.1% on the week and snapping a three-week losing streak** (MarketWatch, 27 November, 15:02 ET; corroborated by Reuters). The FT historical table shows 95.27 for the same date — a different series and print convention, not mixed with the settlement cited here. The connection is mechanism, not forecast: oil is the input to the import bill, the import bill moves the rupee, and the rupee is the currency side of the domestic gold benchmark above.

The flows: **FII/FPI net +₹1,634.33 crore (bought ₹14,259.45 crore, sold ₹12,625.12 crore) and DII net −₹556.42 crore (bought ₹17,263.65 crore, sold ₹17,820.07 crore)** — NSE provisional, read 28 November 07:38 IST; final FPI numbers from NSDL can differ. The two nets ran in opposite directions on the same session: foreign investors bought a net ₹1,634.33 crore while domestic institutions sold a net ₹556.42 crore.

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

### The RBI's 27 November package is real and substantial — six KYC amendments, three payment-system Directions and a CRR change — and not one instrument in it binds an NBFC lender
The RBI's press-release listing, read 07:33 IST, opens at a 27 November block of eleven items, of which the only rule instrument is the money-mule press release; the other ten are liquidity, auction and statistical releases (two VRR auctions and their results, state-loan and T-bill auctions, an underwriting auction and result, a WSS extract, money-market operations and a Standing Advisory Committee meeting notice). The 26 November block holds eight items and the 25 November block ten, all of them operations and releases. The newest notifications block, dated 27 November 2026, carries the money-mule package: **six KYC amendment directions — Payment Banks; Urban Co-operative Banks (Second); Regional Rural Banks (Second); Local Area Banks (Second); Small Finance Banks (Second); Commercial Banks (Second) — every one addressed to banks and co-operative banks, with no non-banking financial company instrument in the set.** The directions institute a standard operating procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected of money-mule activity, effective 1 July 2027 or such earlier date as a bank may decide. **Nothing dated 27 November changes an NBFC lending rule, and the bank SOP creates no obligation for Muthoot Fincorp.** The same block carries three payment-system Directions — White Label ATM Operators; Cash Withdrawal Transactions through ATM and PoS Terminals; Digital Payments - Card-based transaction (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/477) — consolidations binding payment system participants under the PSS Act that reach an NBFC only in a card-issuing or acquiring capacity; and a Section 42(1) notification cutting the CRR daily-maintenance minimum from 99% to 90% for the fortnight beginning 1 December 2026, addressed to All Scheduled Banks — a bank liquidity measure. SEBI's newest circular is dated 27 November — FPI Participation in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives — whose body was not readable from this host and is listed, not summarised. IBBI's page yielded no dated item newer than the 26 November Chairperson appointment already reported. **The deliberate contrast — the 23 November securitisation set that DID include an NBFC instrument, still open at 1 April 2027 — is drawn in full in the regulation report.**

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none from the 27 November package; the newest instrument touching the company's lending business remains the 23 November NBFC securitisation amendment, covered earlier and carried in the deadlines.

## 🏢 Muthoot Fincorp in the market

### The investor page re-read: 873 documents, unchanged for the fourth consecutive edition — no rotation this time, simply no change
Muthoot Fincorp's investor page was re-read through the gated route at 07:01 IST (HTTP 200, 2,770,322 bytes) and shows **no new filing seen: 873 distinct document names — deduplicated on the S3 basenames — unchanged from 27 November, and unchanged on each of the four consecutive editions: 873 on 25, 26, 27 and 28 November.** Unlike the last edition, where one e-auction notice rotated out and one in on the same count, **this time the count is simply unchanged — no document rotation is described here, because none was seen.** The phrasing remains "no new filing seen", never "nothing was filed": the announcements list is partly loaded by script, and an item could still post later in the day or after the weekend.

The EGM trail is unchanged and still unreadable: **the intimation of the EGM to be held on 23 November 2026 (Intimation_of_EGM_to_be_held_on_November_23_2026_b16194d248.pdf) and the Proceedings of the EGM held on 23 November 2026 are on the page, named, and their contents are not readable from here** — the presigned S3 links carry a 900-second expiry baked at page-build time and have expired, and the mflprodweb bucket refuses unsigned requests, directly and through the route. This edition reports that the two documents exist, with their names and dates, and nothing more: what the meeting resolved is in the Proceedings, and until that document is readable, guessing its business — borrowing limits, preference shares, directors, the IPO — would be fabrication, and none is attempted.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none asserted; the page state is recorded as read, and the EGM record stands as held, with its papers posted and unreadable.

reports.content:
# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Saturday, 28 November 2026 (IST)

Weekend edition for 28 November 2026 (IST), covering Friday 27 November to Saturday morning; regulator pages read 07:31–07:38 IST. **The RBI issued six KYC amendment directions dated 27 November, and every one binds banks — payment banks, urban co-operative banks, regional rural banks, local area banks, small finance banks and commercial banks; there is no non-banking financial company instrument in the set.** The money-mule SOP those directions institute — temporary debit holds on suspected mule accounts, effective 1 July 2027 or earlier at a bank's option — creates no obligation for Muthoot Fincorp, and this report does not import a bank SOP into an NBFC rulebook. The contrast with 23 November is deliberate: that day's four parallel securitisation amendments did include an NBFC instrument, still open at 1 April 2027 — the same RBI habit of issuing parallel instruments by lender class, working in the opposite direction this time. **Nothing dated 26, 27 or 28 November changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.**

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

### RBI: six KYC amendment directions dated 27 November — the money-mule SOP, binding banks and co-operative banks only
The RBI's notifications listing, read 07:33 IST, opens its 27 November 2026 block with six items in list order: **the (Payment Banks - KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, and five Second Amendment Directions, 2026 — Urban Co-operative Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Local Area Banks, Small Finance Banks and Commercial Banks** — each titled "RBI (... - KYC)". The press release beside them (prid=64062) states the content: **a standard operating procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected of money-mule activity; drafts were issued 11 September 2026 for stakeholder feedback; a feedback statement accompanies the final directions; effective 1 July 2027, or such earlier date as a bank may decide.**

**These instruments bind banks and co-operative banks only; no NBFC instrument exists in the set.** Nothing dated 27 November changes an NBFC lending rule, the money-mule SOP creates no obligation for Muthoot Fincorp, and this report does not read a bank SOP into an NBFC rulebook. The deliberate contrast is 23 November: **the four parallel securitisation amendments — AIFIs (Id=13756), NBFCs (Id=13755), Small Finance Banks (Id=13754), Commercial Banks (Id=13753), effective 1 April 2027 — did include the NBFC instrument, still open in the deadlines below.**

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none from this package.
Sources: [RBI notifications, 27 Nov 2026 block](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [RBI money-mule press release, prid=64062](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=64062)

### RBI: CRR daily-maintenance minimum falls from 99% to 90% — a bank liquidity measure
Also on the 27 November block, under **Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934 (Id=13759): the minimum daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio falls from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent, from the fortnight beginning 1 December 2026.** Addressed to **All Scheduled Banks**, citing reference circular **DoR.RET.REC.247/12.01.001/2026-27 dated 9 October 2026**, signed J P Sharma, Chief General Manager-in-Charge — a bank liquidity measure, not an NBFC rule, and not a company deadline below.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none — the instrument is addressed to scheduled banks.
Sources: [RBI notification, Id=13759](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13759&Mode=0)

### RBI: three payment-system Directions dated 27 November — consolidations under the PSS Act
Three Directions on the same block: **White Label ATM Operators; Cash Withdrawal Transactions through ATM and PoS Terminals; and Digital Payments - Card-based transaction — the last carrying reference RBI/DPSS/2026-27/477, CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S910/02-14-001/2026-2027, dated 27 November 2026, addressed to "Authorised Payment System Providers and System Participants (Banks and Non Banks)".** The card-based instrument **consolidates 25 existing card circulars into one and is effective immediately from issuance**; the three bind payment system providers and participants under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 — **consolidations, not new obligations, reaching an NBFC only in a card-issuing or acquiring capacity, not its gold-loan lending business.** No reference numbers were visible for the first two.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none on the lending business; in a card-issuing or acquiring capacity the consolidated instrument is the operative text.
Sources: [RBI notifications, 27 Nov 2026 block](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [Card-based Directions PDF](https://rbidocs.rbi.org.in/rdocs/notification/PDFs/477MD27112026EF6EF971FB54489288F4B731B409D9CE.PDF)

### SEBI: FPI ETCD circular dated 27 November — listed and scoped, not summarised
SEBI's circulars listing, read 07:31 IST via the phone route (HTTP 200, 45,401 bytes), carries one 27 November item: **"FPI Participation in Exchange Traded Commodity Derivatives (ETCDs)"** — scope as listed: FPIs and exchange traded commodity derivatives, **no NBFC lending obligation created.** The page body is JS-rendered and returned only the title to this host, so **the operative paragraphs were not read and are not summarised; the instrument is listed with its date and scope, nothing more.**

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated; the operative text was not readable from here.
Sources: [SEBI circulars listing](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0) · [SEBI: FPI Participation in ETCDs, 27 Nov 2026](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/fpi-participation-in-exchange-traded-commodity-derivatives-etcds-_105989.html)

### RBI: two UAPA sanctions-list amendments dated 26 November — carried, no change
Carried from the 27 November edition: **two amendments under Section 51A of UAPA implementing updates to the UNSC's 1267/1989 ISIL (Da'esh) & Al-Qaida Sanctions List — Id=13758 amending one entry, Id=13757 amending 81 entries.** Sanctions-list maintenance binds regulated entities for customer screening — a KYC obligation across regulated entities including NBFCs, not a lending rule.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: an updated sanctions list is an input to customer screening; no lending rule applying to the company changed.
Sources: [RBI notifications, 26 Nov 2026 block](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx)

## 📖 The standing rulebook: the LTV bands, unchanged; AGLOC's new block runs 28-30 November
The gold-loan LTV bands this week's reporting rests on are the standing ones: **85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% between ₹2.5 and 5 lakh, 75% above ₹5 lakh — effective 1 April 2026 — with LTV maintained through the loan tenure and a breach treated as default even without a missed payment.** **No RBI instrument dated 26, 27 or 28 November changes them, and nothing on the 27 November block touches any other rule applying to Muthoot Fincorp's lending business.** What moved is the published ceiling: **AGLOC's new block — headed 30 November 2026 and dated 28-30 November on its own table, so it carries this weekend and Monday rather than Monday alone — puts the bands at ₹9,833 at 85%, ₹9,255 at 80% and ₹8,676 at 75%, on a jewellery reference of ₹11,569** — ₹285, ₹268 and ₹251 above the 27 November block, the reference up ₹336. The reference is a mechanical re-strike, not new discovery: **₹11,569 is IBJA's 27 November PM 916 rate ÷ 10 exactly**, and **the bands move together because they are fixed percentages of the one reference — one observation, not three**.

Beside the bands sits one representation, not a rule: **ET reported on 26 November that banks and gold-loan companies such as Muthoot and Manappuram have informed the RBI that, as a prudential measure, they have lowered the LTV on fresh loans to an average of 60–65% from about 75%.** ET names "Muthoot" without saying which entity — Muthoot Finance is the listed company; Muthoot Fincorp is not named — and a representation to the RBI is not a rule change: **the RBI has not relaxed or cut anything; the bands stand, and writing below them is prudential discretion, not a requirement.**

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: these bands and this reference govern the ceiling the company lends under — ₹9,833 at the 85% band for the block running 28-30 November, ₹285 above the previous block; nothing about the company's own book is inferred from either.
Sources: [AGLOC, block headed 30 Nov 2026, dated 28-30 Nov](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/) · [Financial Express, 23 Nov 2026 — the standing bands](https://www.financialexpress.com/market/gold-loan-lenders-face-collateral-pressure-as-prices-slide-4391109/) · [Economic Times, 26 Nov 05:30 IST](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/banking/gold-crash-triggers-auction-notices-as-ltv-breaches-hit-lenders/articleshow/136172114.cms)

## What was checked

The RBI's press-release listing, read 07:33 IST on 28 November (HTTP 200), opens at a 27 November 2026 block of eleven items, of which only the money-mule press release (prid=64062) is a rule instrument — the rest are VRR auctions and results, state-loan and T-bill auctions, an underwriting auction and result, a WSS extract, money-market operations and a Standing Advisory Committee notice; below it, 26 November holds a 3-day VRR and Reserve Money and Money Supply for the fortnight ended 15 November, and 25 November an overnight VRR — operations and statistics, no rules. The notifications listing, read 07:33 IST (HTTP 200), opens at a 27 November block of ten items in list order — the six KYC amendments, the three payment-system Directions (the card-based one carrying RBI/DPSS/2026-27/477) and the Section 42(1) CRR change (Id=13759); below it, the 26 November UAPA pair (Id=13758, 81 entries; Id=13757, 01 entry) and the 23 November securitisation quartet (NBFC Id=13755 among the four, effective 1 April 2027, covered earlier — for an NBFC, the NBFC one is the operative text). SEBI's circulars listing was read 07:31 IST via the phone route, direct DNS failing on this host (HTTP 200, 45,401 bytes): newest is the 27 November FPI ETCD circular, body JS-rendered and not readable from here — listed and scoped, not summarised; below it, the 25 November pair covered earlier and the 17 November margin-framework review. IBBI's homepage was read on 28 November (HTTP 200, 1,613,599 bytes), JS-heavy, with no dated item newer than the 26 November Chairperson appointment extractable — no new IBBI item is recorded, a statement about what was extractable, not a claim that nothing was published.

## Latest circulars (last 10 days)

cards.summary: The collateral picture reversed direction on Friday. Front-month Comex gold for December delivery — the new front month — settled at $3,639.60 an ounce, up $103.80 or 2.94% on the day and 3.53% on the week (Dow Jones Market Data via Morningstar, 27 November).
cards.impact: a higher gold price raises the collateral value behind gold loans across lenders, including Muthoot Fincorp, on every ticket at once. The equity moves belong to the listed companies whose tickers printed them — Muthoot Finance, Manappuram and IIFL Finance are listed peers — and Muthoot Fincorp is unlisted, with no share price in either index; nothing about the company's own book is inferred from Friday's session.
